fields.text: A purse marked Php 1,200 is sold at 20% off, then an extra 10% off the sale price. What is the final price?
fields.explanation: 20% off leaves 0.80 × ₱1,200 = ₱960; the extra 10% off leaves 0.90 × ₱960 = ₱864. Successive discounts are not simply added.
fields.steps:
1. First discount: 0.80 × ₱1,200 = ₱960.
2. Second discount is on ₱960: 0.90 × ₱960 = ₱864.
3. Final price: ₱864.
fields.hint: The second discount is taken from the sale price, not from the marked price.
fields.whyB: ₱840 adds the discounts into one 30% off; the 10% applies only to the reduced price.
fields.whyC: ₱960 applies only the first 20% discount.
fields.whyD: ₱900 is a straight 25% discount; neither step gives that.
fields.explanationTl: Pagkatapos ng 20% off, ₱960 na lang. Tapos 10% off ulit sa ₱960, kaya ₱864. Hindi pwedeng i-add lang ang 20% at 10%.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Unang discount: 0.80 × ₱1,200 = ₱960.
2. Ang pangalawang discount ay sa ₱960: 0.90 × ₱960 = ₱864.
3. Final price: ₱864.
fields.hintTl: Ang second discount ay kinukuha sa sale price, hindi sa original na presyo.

fields.text: A bus travels 180 km at 60 km/h, then another 100 km at 50 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?

fields.text: Two buses 150 km apart start at the same time and drive toward each other at 40 km/h and 35 km/h. After how many hours will they meet?

fields.stepsTl:
1. Magkasalubong: i-add ang speeds, 40 + 35 = 75 km/h.
2. Time = layo ÷ combined speed = 150 ÷ 75.
3. 2 hours.
fields.hintTl: Pag magkasalubong ang dalawang sasakyan, umiikli ang gap sa sum ng speeds nila.

reason: One of ten near-identical 'n workers, n items, n time' items; rewritten as a worker-hours rate problem.

fields.text: 4 bakers bake 24 cakes in 3 hours. At the same rate, how many cakes can 6 bakers bake in 5 hours?
fields.explanation: One baker bakes 24 ÷ (4 × 3) = 2 cakes per hour, so 6 bakers in 5 hours bake 6 × 5 × 2 = 60 cakes.
fields.steps:
1. Baker-hours used: 4 × 3 = 12.
2. Cakes per baker-hour: 24 ÷ 12 = 2.
3. New baker-hours: 6 × 5 = 30.
4. Cakes: 30 × 2 = 60.
fields.hint: Find how much ONE worker does per unit of time first.
fields.whyA: 40 scales only by the hours (24 × 5/3) and forgets the extra bakers.
fields.whyC: 36 scales only by the bakers (24 × 6/4) and forgets the extra hours.
fields.whyD: 72 triples 24; the correct factor is 6/4 × 5/3 = 2.5.
fields.explanationTl: Isang baker = 24 ÷ (4 × 3) = 2 cakes per hour. Kaya 6 bakers × 5 hours × 2 = 60 cakes.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Baker-hours: 4 × 3 = 12.
2. Cakes per baker-hour: 24 ÷ 12 = 2.
3. Bagong baker-hours: 6 × 5 = 30.
4. Cakes: 30 × 2 = 60.
fields.hintTl: Alamin muna kung gaano karami ang natatapos ng ISANG worker per unit ng oras.

reason: One of ten near-identical 'n workers, n items, n time' items; rewritten as a working-together problem.

fields.text: A mechanic can overhaul an engine in 6 hours; his helper needs 12 hours. Working together, how many hours will they take?
fields.explanation: Together they do 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the job per hour, so they need 4 hours.
fields.steps:
1. Mechanic: 1/6 job per hour. Helper: 1/12 job per hour.
2. Together: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 1/4 = 4 hours.
fields.hint: Add the hourly rates (fractions of the job), not the hours.
fields.whyA: 9 averages 6 and 12; working together must be faster than either alone.
fields.whyB: 6 is the mechanic's time alone; the helper's work makes it faster.
fields.whyD: 3 halves the mechanic's time, as if the helper were just as fast.
fields.explanationTl: Sabay sila: 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/4 ng trabaho kada oras, kaya 4 hours.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Mechanic: 1/6 per hour. Helper: 1/12 per hour.
2. Sabay: 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/4 per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 1/4 = 4 hours.
fields.hintTl: I-add ang rates (fraction ng trabaho kada oras), hindi ang hours.

fields.hint: More workers means FEWER days: find the total worker-days first.
fields.whyA: 9 treats it as direct proportion (6 × 12 ÷ 8); more artists should take less time.
fields.whyB: 3 halves the time, as if the artists doubled; 12 is only 1.5 times 8.
fields.whyC: 5 just subtracts one day; it does not use the 48 artist-days.
fields.explanationTl: Ang mural ay 8 × 6 = 48 artist-days. Kaya 48 ÷ 12 = 4 days.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Total work: 8 × 6 = 48 artist-days.
2. 12 artists: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 days.
fields.hintTl: Mas maraming workers, mas KAUNTING days. Hanapin muna ang total worker-days.

reason: One of ten near-identical 'n workers, n items, n time' items; rewritten as workers leaving midway.

fields.text: 12 painters can finish painting a building in 10 days. After 4 days, 4 painters leave. How many MORE days will the rest need to finish?
fields.explanation: The job is 12 × 10 = 120 painter-days; 48 are done in 4 days, leaving 72, which 8 painters finish in 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days.
fields.steps:
1. Total work: 12 × 10 = 120 painter-days.
2. Done in 4 days: 12 × 4 = 48.
3. Left: 120 − 48 = 72 painter-days.
4. Painters left: 12 − 4 = 8.
5. More days: 72 ÷ 8 = 9.
fields.hint: Count the work in painter-days, subtract what is done, then divide by the painters who remain.
fields.whyB: 6 is the days left if all 12 painters stayed.
fields.whyC: 8 is the number of painters left, not the number of days.
fields.whyD: 12 divides the remaining work by 6 painters instead of 8.
fields.explanationTl: Ang trabaho ay 12 × 10 = 120 painter-days. Tapos na ang 48 sa 4 days, kaya 72 na lang. 72 ÷ 8 painters = 9 days.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Total: 12 × 10 = 120 painter-days.
2. Natapos sa 4 days: 12 × 4 = 48.
3. Natira: 120 − 48 = 72.
4. Natirang painters: 8.
5. 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days pa.
fields.hintTl: Bilangin ang trabaho in painter-days, ibawas ang tapos na, tapos i-divide sa natirang painters.

reason: duplicate of 1773526566; rewritten as pipe fills in 2 h, drain empties in 5 h (3 1/3 h)

fields.text: A pipe can fill a tank in 2 hours, and a drain can empty the full tank in 5 hours. If both are open, how many hours will it take to fill the empty tank?
fields.explanation: Each hour the tank gains 1/2 − 1/5 = 3/10 of its volume, so it fills in 10/3 = 3 1/3 hours (3 hours 20 minutes).
fields.steps:
1. Pipe: +1/2 tank per hour. Drain: −1/5 tank per hour.
2. Net: 1/2 − 1/5 = 5/10 − 2/10 = 3/10 tank per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 3/10 = 10/3 hours.
4. 10/3 = 3 1/3 hours (3 hours 20 minutes).
fields.hint: The drain works against the pipe, so subtract its rate.
fields.whyA: 1 3/7 hours adds the rates (1/2 + 1/5 = 7/10) as if the drain were also filling.
fields.whyC: 7 hours just adds the two times.
fields.whyD: 3 hours subtracts the times (5 − 2) instead of the rates.
fields.explanationTl: Kada oras, napupuno ng 1/2 pero nababawasan ng 1/5, kaya net 3/10 per hour. 10/3 = 3 1/3 hours bago mapuno.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Pipe: +1/2 per hour. Drain: −1/5 per hour.
2. Net: 1/2 − 1/5 = 5/10 − 2/10 = 3/10 per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 3/10 = 10/3 hours.
4. 10/3 = 3 1/3 hours (3 hours 20 minutes).
fields.hintTl: Kumokontra ang drain sa pipe, kaya i-subtract ang rate nito.

reason: Exact duplicate of 476935905's original (5 workers, 5 jobs, 5 days, same options); rewritten as finding one worker's time.

fields.text: Rosa can clean a hall alone in 5 hours. With Liza helping, they finish in 3 hours. How many hours would Liza need alone?
fields.explanation: Together they do 1/3 per hour and Rosa does 1/5, so Liza does 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 per hour and needs 15/2 = 7.5 hours.
fields.steps:
1. Together: 1/3 job per hour. Rosa: 1/5 per hour.
2. Liza: 1/3 − 1/5 = 5/15 − 3/15 = 2/15 per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 2/15 = 15/2 = 7.5 hours.
fields.hint: Subtract Rosa's hourly rate from their combined hourly rate.
fields.whyA: 2 subtracts the hours (5 − 3) instead of the rates.
fields.whyB: 8 adds the hours (5 + 3).
fields.whyC: 4 averages 5 and 3; Liza alone must be slower than the pair together.
fields.explanationTl: Sabay sila 1/3 per hour, si Rosa 1/5. Kaya si Liza ay 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 per hour, o 7.5 hours mag-isa.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Sabay: 1/3 per hour. Rosa: 1/5 per hour.
2. Liza: 1/3 − 1/5 = 2/15 per hour.
3. Time = 1 ÷ 2/15 = 7.5 hours.
fields.hintTl: Ibawas ang rate ni Rosa sa combined rate nila.

reason: One of ten near-identical 'n workers, n items, n time' items; rewritten to find the workers needed.

fields.text: 3 tailors sew 15 uniforms in 5 days. At the same rate, how many tailors are needed to sew 36 uniforms in 4 days?
fields.explanation: Each tailor sews 15 ÷ (3 × 5) = 1 uniform a day; 36 uniforms in 4 days need 9 uniforms a day, so 9 tailors.
fields.steps:
1. Tailor-days used: 3 × 5 = 15.
2. Uniforms per tailor-day: 15 ÷ 15 = 1.
3. Needed per day: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 uniforms.
4. Tailors: 9 ÷ 1 = 9.
fields.hint: Find how much ONE worker does per unit of time first.
fields.whyA: 12 divides 36 by 3 (the old number of tailors) instead of using each tailor's daily rate.
fields.whyC: 7 scales only the uniforms (3 × 36/15 ≈ 7.2) and ignores that there are fewer days.
fields.whyD: 8 tailors sew only 32 uniforms in 4 days.
fields.explanationTl: Isang tailor = 1 uniform per day. Para sa 36 uniforms sa 4 days, kailangan ng 9 per day, kaya 9 tailors.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Tailor-days: 3 × 5 = 15.
2. Uniforms per tailor-day: 15 ÷ 15 = 1.
3. Kailangan kada araw: 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
4. Tailors: 9.
fields.hintTl: Alamin muna kung gaano karami ang natatapos ng ISANG worker per unit ng oras.

reason: One of ten near-identical 'n workers, n items, n time' items ('studying chapters' isn't shared work); rewritten as a join-midway problem.

fields.text: Carlo can finish a job alone in 10 days. He works alone for 4 days, then Dan joins him and together they finish the rest in 3 days. How many days would Dan need to do the whole job alone?
fields.explanation: Carlo does 4/10 in 4 days, leaving 6/10; together they do 6/10 ÷ 3 = 1/5 per day, so Dan does 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 per day and needs 10 days alone.
fields.steps:
1. Carlo's rate: 1/10 per day; in 4 days he does 4/10.
2. Left: 1 − 4/10 = 6/10.
3. Together: 6/10 ÷ 3 = 2/10 = 1/5 per day.
4. Dan: 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 per day.
5. Dan alone: 10 days.
fields.hint: Find what is left after Carlo's 4 days, then the pair's daily rate.
fields.whyB: 15 forgets Carlo's share in the last 3 days and treats the 6/10 as Dan's work alone.
fields.whyC: 12 assumes Dan is slower than Carlo; their rates turn out equal.
fields.whyD: 6 is the days Carlo alone would still need, not Dan's time for the whole job.
fields.explanationTl: Sa 4 days, 4/10 ang natapos ni Carlo, natira 6/10. Sabay nilang tinapos sa 3 days, kaya 1/5 per day. Si Dan ay 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 per day, kaya 10 days mag-isa.
fields.stepsTl:
1. Carlo: 1/10 per day; sa 4 days, 4/10.
2. Natira: 6/10.
3. Sabay: 6/10 ÷ 3 = 1/5 per day.
4. Dan: 1/5 − 1/10 = 1/10 per day.
5. Dan mag-isa: 10 days.
fields.hintTl: Alamin kung gaano karami ang natira pagkatapos ng 4 days ni Carlo, tapos ang daily rate nilang dalawa.
